Wing and Walmart plan Denver and Seattle drone deliveries in 2027

Two new metro areas join a network plan approaching 20 markets and more than 270 stores; service has not yet launched in the new regions.

Wing ↗5 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Two additional metropolitan markets

Wing and Walmart announced on October 5 that Denver and Seattle will join their delivery network in 2027, bringing the expansion plan close to 20 major US metro areas. The partners say more than three million customers already have access in markets including Dallas–Fort Worth, Atlanta, Houston and Orlando. Access is not the same as a count of actual ordering customers.

Network scale and different climates

The broader plan targets more than 270 Walmart locations and access for over 40 million customers. Seattle’s rain and Denver’s wintry conditions extend the range of operating environments. Wing says its aircraft can travel up to 60 mph and carry up to five pounds. The announcement does not imply unrestricted operation in every weather condition.

Ordering when service becomes available

Eligible customers will see drone delivery in Walmart’s app and website, with ordering also available through Wing’s app. Supported items include groceries and household goods, subject to local availability. The 2027 timing remains a rollout plan and does not establish that every home in Denver or Seattle will be within range from the first day.
